proof:
Source: step 0(a), (b) and (d) of the parent proof (local Lipschitz bounds for the C¹ map G), isolated for an arbitrary S ⊆ D and with the details filled in. Notation: H^m := μHE[m] (on ℝ^d and on ℝ^P), |·| the Euclidean norms.

1. (G is locally Lipschitz on D.) Let x ∈ D. Since D is open, choose r > 0 with closedBall(x, 2r) ⊆ D. G is C¹ on the open set D, so G is differentiable on D and DG is continuous on D; hence ‖DG‖ is bounded on the compact set closedBall(x, 2r), say by L_x. This ball is convex, so the mean value inequality gives |G(v) − G(v′)| ≤ L_x|v − v′| for all v, v′ ∈ closedBall(x, 2r). (Equivalently: G is C¹ at x because D is a neighbourhood of x, so G is Lipschitz on a neighbourhood of x; Mathlib ContDiffAt.exists_lipschitzOnWith.)

2. (Proof of (i).) Let K ⊆ D be compact. If K = ∅ every L works. Otherwise the open balls B(x, r_x), x ∈ K, of step 1 cover K; take a finite subcover B(x_1, r_1), …, B(x_N, r_N) with constants L_1, …, L_N valid on closedBall(x_k, 2r_k). Put ρ := min_k r_k > 0, L₀ := max_k L_k and M_K := sup_{v∈K} |G(v)| < ∞ (G is continuous on the compact set K). Let v, v′ ∈ K. If |v − v′| < ρ, pick k with v ∈ B(x_k, r_k); then |v′ − x_k| < r_k + ρ ≤ 2r_k, so v, v′ ∈ closedBall(x_k, 2r_k) and |G(v) − G(v′)| ≤ L₀|v − v′|. If |v − v′| ≥ ρ, then |G(v) − G(v′)| ≤ 2M_K ≤ (2M_K/ρ)|v − v′|. Hence G is L-Lipschitz on K with L := max(L₀, 2M_K/ρ). (This is Mathlib LocallyLipschitzOn.exists_lipschitzOnWith_of_compact applied to the locally Lipschitz map of step 1.)

3. (Countable compact exhaustion of D.) There are compact sets K_j ⊆ D, j ∈ ℕ, with D = ⋃_j K_j. Indeed, if D = ∅ take K_j := ∅. Otherwise choose for each x ∈ D some s_x > 0 with closedBall(x, s_x) ⊆ D; the open balls B(x, s_x) cover D, and since ℝ^d is second countable (Lindelöf), countably many of them, B(x_j, s_j) (j ∈ ℕ), still cover D. Put K_j := closedBall(x_j, s_j), which is compact (Heine–Borel) and contained in D. (In Lean: the open subset D of the locally compact, second-countable space ℝ^d is a locally compact second-countable subspace, hence σ-compact; IsOpen.locallyCompactSpace and isSigmaCompact_iff_sigmaCompactSpace give K_j compact with ⋃_j K_j = D.) By (i) choose L_j ≥ 0 such that G is L_j-Lipschitz on K_j. For every S ⊆ D we have S = ⋃_j (S ∩ K_j), hence G(S) = ⋃_j G(S ∩ K_j).

4. (Lipschitz image bound.) If f is L-Lipschitz on an arbitrary set A, then H^m(f(A)) ≤ L^m · H^m(A) for the Euclidean-normalized Hausdorff measure; no measurability of A is needed (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn).

5. (Proof of (ii).) Let S ⊆ D with H^m(S) = 0. For each j, G is L_j-Lipschitz on S ∩ K_j ⊆ K_j, so by step 4, H^m(G(S ∩ K_j)) ≤ L_j^m · H^m(S ∩ K_j) ≤ L_j^m · H^m(S) = 0. By step 3 and countable subadditivity, H^m(G(S)) ≤ Σ_j H^m(G(S ∩ K_j)) = 0.

6. (Proof of (iii).) Let S ⊆ D be countably m-rectifiable: there are M₀ ⊆ ℝ^d with H^m(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps Ψ_k : ℝ^m → ℝ^d (k ∈ ℕ) with S ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_k Ψ_k(ℝ^m). Fix j. Because ℝ^P is finite-dimensional, the L_j-Lipschitz map G|_{K_j} extends to a Lipschitz map G̃_j : ℝ^d → ℝ^P with G̃_j = G on K_j (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_finite_dimension; e.g. extend each coordinate by McShane's formula); let L̃_j be a Lipschitz constant of G̃_j. Then
 G(S ∩ K_j) = G̃_j(S ∩ K_j) ⊆ G̃_j(M₀) ∪ ⋃_k (G̃_j ∘ Ψ_k)(ℝ^m):
 for x ∈ S ∩ K_j we have G(x) = G̃_j(x); if x ∈ M₀ then G̃_j(x) ∈ G̃_j(M₀), and if x = Ψ_k(y) then G̃_j(x) = (G̃_j ∘ Ψ_k)(y).
 By step 4 (with A := M₀ and f := G̃_j), H^m(G̃_j(M₀)) ≤ L̃_j^m · H^m(M₀) = 0, and every G̃_j ∘ Ψ_k : ℝ^m → ℝ^P is Lipschitz as a composition of Lipschitz maps. So G(S ∩ K_j) satisfies the definition of countable m-rectifiability (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable) with exceptional set G̃_j(M₀) and parametrizations G̃_j ∘ Ψ_k, k ∈ ℕ.
 By step 3, G(S) = ⋃_j G(S ∩ K_j) is a countable union of countably m-rectifiable sets and is therefore countably m-rectifiable: the union of the countably many null exceptional sets is null, and the countably many parametrizations indexed by (j, k) ∈ ℕ × ℕ are re-indexed by ℕ (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_iUnion). ∎
key_steps: A C¹ map on an open set is Lipschitz on a closed ball around each point of D (mean value inequality), hence locally Lipschitz on D.
A locally Lipschitz map is Lipschitz on each compact K ⊆ D (finite subcover, ρ := min r_k, the bound 2 sup_K|G| for distant pairs): conclusion (i).
D is a countable union of compact sets K_j ⊆ D (Lindelöf / σ-compactness), so G(S) = ⋃_j G(S ∩ K_j) for S ⊆ D.
The Lipschitz image bound H^m(G(S ∩ K_j)) ≤ L_j^m H^m(S ∩ K_j) and countable subadditivity give conclusion (ii).
Extending G|_{K_j} to a global Lipschitz G̃_j, G(S ∩ K_j) ⊆ G̃_j(M₀) ∪ ⋃_k range(G̃_j ∘ Ψ_k) is countably rectifiable; the countable union over j gives conclusion (iii).
